clue.text: As a pond thaws out, entering empty river

indicators.note: entering signals the shuffled letters going inside the other word

parts.note: to free a room of its contents is to empty it

indicators.note: out signals the letters of thaws are put out of order

explanation.surface: A frozen pond melting while a dried-up river runs into it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Empty' here means free of contents, giving FREE; 'out' shuffles the thaws letters before they go 'entering'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pond holds fresh rather than salt water, so the phrase describes its kind of water.

clue.text: In conversation, witty person overcomes tiresome one, the beast

explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'overcomes' puts WILDE above BORE; said together they sound like the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild boar is a beast, the untamed pig of European forests.

clue.text: Delivery of orders at regular intervals, prompt

parts.note: a couple is a pair

explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges the letters of signed, and 'parting' sends the couple between them; 'signed off' is not a farewell.

clue.text: Sweet thing in well gripping game, a hundred ahead

indicators.note: gripping means holding something inside

parts.note: well, in good health, means fit
RU is rugby union, a game

explanation.walkthrough: 'gripping' holds the game inside well; 'in' is a link word, and RU (rugby union) is a common crossword game.
explanation.definitionFit: A fruit cup is a dessert of mixed fruit, so a sweet in the pudding sense.

clue.text: African capital where monarch renounces name Muhammad

clue.text: In Badagara, I take a dip in India

parts.words: In which one may be driven to drink

indicators.note: sound signals a word that is heard rather than read

parts.note: the witching hour is midnight, when witches are said to be about

explanation.definitionFit: Twitching is an involuntary jerking, as when an eyelid flickers or blinks.

clue.text: Semisweet item is cut with one bite taken out

indicators.note: taken out signals letters removed from their order and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
a means one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A biscuit cut up with one bite missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken out' rearranges IS CUT, A and BITE.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea biscuit is a plain, lightly sweetened biscuit eaten with tea.

clue.text: Author holds US state up not as a harmless native of America

indicators.note: holds means contains another piece within

parts.note: Graham Greene, English novelist

indicators.note: up reverses the piece in a down entry
not means a piece is left out

parts.note: Kansas is a US state
taken as written

definitions.text: make old tender thing feel sexy?

clue.text: Totally blissful condition's ending in vicar getting drunk

getting drunk signals letters reeling into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: 'ending' takes N from 'condition's'; 'getting drunk' rearranges IN VICAR into IRVANIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Nirvanic describes nirvana, the Buddhist state of perfect bliss.

clue.text: Further adjusting compound interest, grand goes on

indicators.note: goes on means is added afterwards
compound means to mix, so the letters are combined in new order

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand

the head, or first letter, of this poet's own name

clue.text: Where suspects held without trial, bear it in mind

taken as written

definitions.meaning: a moan or grumble, a complaint
